Gemini said

Great choice of problem! "Return kth to last" (often phrased as finding the n-th node from the end of a linked list) is a quintessential interview question for mastering the Two-Pointer technique.

From the exact list you provided, here are the absolute best places to practice this specific problem in Python, mapped to how they name it:

1. NeetCode.io

  • Problem Name: Remove Nth Node From End of List

  • Why it's great: While this version asks you to remove the node rather than just returning it, it relies on the exact same underlying logic. To remove it, you first have to find it using the two-pointer approach. NeetCode provides a clean interface and fantastic Python video/text explanations.

2. GeeksforGeeks.org

  • Problem Name: Kth from End of Linked List

  • Why it's great: This is an exact 1:1 match to the Cracking the Coding Interview problem. You are given the head of a linked list and a number k, and your job is to find and return the data of that node using Python.

3. InterviewBit.com

  • Problem Name: Remove Nth Node from List End

  • Why it's great: Like NeetCode, this requires you to delete the node, but it has excellent constraints and testing environments tailored heavily toward actual tech interview scenarios.

💡 A Quick Tip for Your Practice

When transitioning from the book to these sites, keep an eye on how they define index k:

  • Some platforms consider the last node to be the 1-st to last (k=1).

  • Others use 0-based indexing, where the last node is the 0-th to last (k=0).

Adjust your pointer gaps accordingly!

Note: The other sites on your list (like Codeforces, Project Euler, or AtCoder) focus heavily on competitive programming, math, or basic language tracks, and won't have this specific classic linked list interview question.
